items.title: Air India’s Losses Are Still Bigger Than Singapore Airlines’ Profit
items.summary: Singapore Airlines’ India bet is costly. Losses are shrinking, but the stake only pays off if Air India fixes its costs. Until then, the profitable core airline is footing the bill.

items.title: Mantis Keeps Building in Gulf as Demand Shrinks to Locals
items.summary: The war means Mantis’ Gulf properties are serving only a domestic market for now. Its long-term bet on the region, as it builds out its "circuit" tourism offer, depends on international travelers coming back.

items.title: Dusit Takes Low-Risk Bet on Yangon as Others Retreat
items.summary: Dusit, a Thai hotels and hospitality group, is entering Myanmar as others write off projects and close hotels, but on terms that limit its exposure: management contracts on existing hotels, a focus on business travel, and outside checks on the owner. If leisure demand stays weak,

items.title: MCR’s Tyler Morse Wants to Ban AI Bots From Booking His Hotels
items.summary: MCR Hotels CEO and Chairman Tyler Morse dislikes AI personal assistants because they "make more rational decisions." He prefers human customers, who can more easily be persuaded to make impulse purchases.

items.title: Citi Says AI Companies Should Pay When Their Agents Book the Wrong Travel
items.summary: AI agents are already booking travel, and they get things wrong. The industry hasn’t settled who absorbs the cost when they do. Citi wants the agent companies on the hook, which would spare hotels and airlines, but could slow how fast agents transact.

items.title: United Airlines Moves to Block Personal AI Agents From Booking Flights
items.summary: United is the first carrier in the U.S. to explicitly say it will restrict access to third-party AI agents.

items.title: Scandic’s Dalata Deal Just Got Its First Report Card
items.summary: Scandic paid €500 million for a business that fills more rooms and earns more per room than its own operation. The first combined numbers back the deal. The test now is whether it can integrate slowly enough to protect the occupancy that made Dalata worth buying.

items.title: Playing Catch-Up: Can American Close the Gap With Delta and United?
items.summary: American is the biggest U.S. airline but the least profitable of the Big Three. The changes underway are widespread: from new routes and premium offerings to Tate’s cookies.
